comment: Machine-readable rules derived from reference/tells-register.md. Every rule id maps to a register entry. Weights follow the measured evidence in research file 04 (12 verified AI-generated repos) and the register's verification pass.

provenance.name: Lovable scaffold
provenance.explain: This is Lovable's own plumbing. It only appears in projects Lovable generated.
provenance.fix: Nothing to fix by itself - but it proves the project is AI-generated, so run the full scan and fix what it finds.

provenance.name: v0 placeholder images
provenance.explain: These exact placeholder image URLs are emitted by v0 (and sometimes Lovable). Humans use real images or picsum.
provenance.fix: Replace every placeholder image with a real screenshot, photo, or a deliberately chosen illustration.

provenance.name: v0 sync README
provenance.fix: Write a README in your own words.

provenance.name: Bolt template config
provenance.explain: Bolt.new writes this template marker into config.json.
provenance.fix: Proof of generation - run the full scan and fix what it finds.

provenance.name: Replit Agent memory file
provenance.explain: replit.md is the Replit Agent's memory file. (.replit alone only means Replit hosting.)
provenance.fix: Proof of generation - run the full scan and fix what it finds.

provenance.name: Generator comments/meta
provenance.explain: The tool signed its work in a comment or meta tag.
provenance.fix: Remove the comment/meta tag, then fix what the full scan finds.

provenance.name: Chat residue in shipped text
provenance.explain: Text pasted straight from a chat window, or placeholder text that was never replaced.
provenance.fix: Delete it and write the real content.

code_tells.name: Legacy AI purple/indigo accent
code_tells.explain: The classic 'AI purple'. Real in older one-shot output, but measured at 0 of 12 modern AI repos - so it only scores 1 point.
code_tells.fix: Pick an accent colour that belongs to YOUR product (see the design brief template).

code_tells.name: Gradient headline text
code_tells.explain: Headline words filled with a gradient. Rare in hand-written code, common in AI output - and its contrast can't be verified for accessibility.
code_tells.fix: Use a solid text colour. If you want emphasis, change size or weight instead.

code_tells.name: Many two-hue gradient washes
code_tells.explain: 5 or more different colour-to-colour gradients in one project. The hues follow your topic, but the gradient reflex is the tell.
code_tells.fix: Keep at most one gradient, on one focal element - or none.

code_tells.name: Dark hero glass combo
code_tells.explain: Dark background + frosted white-glass cards + blur, together. This exact combination is the 'Claude dark hero' cluster.
code_tells.fix: If you want dark, build depth from typography and surface levels, not glow and glass.

code_tells.name: Glow blobs
code_tells.explain: Big blurred colour blobs floating behind content. Almost never hand-written.
code_tells.fix: Delete the blob divs. Let the content carry the page.

code_tells.name: The 'tasteful cream' escape look
code_tells.explain: Warm cream + serif + terracotta: the look AI tools fled to after purple was called out. Now a tell itself.
code_tells.fix: Nothing wrong with warm neutrals - but choose them for a reason you can name, and change at least the pairing.

code_tells.name: The 2025 slop font pairing
code_tells.explain: Inter + Space Grotesk or Inter + Instrument Serif is the recurring 2025-era AI pairing.
code_tells.fix: Pick a display face with a reason behind it, and name it in your design brief.

code_tells.name: Italic serif accent word in a sans hero
code_tells.explain: One italic-serif word dropped into a sans headline - the universal AI hero garnish.
code_tells.fix: Either commit to a serif system or drop the garnish.

code_tells.name: ALL-CAPS tracked eyebrow labels
code_tells.explain: Tiny ALL-CAPS labels above every heading. Also harder to read for dyslexic users.
code_tells.fix: Delete eyebrows that say nothing. Keep at most one, only if it carries real information.

code_tells.name: Hero type sandwich
code_tells.explain: The exact 'huge bold tight-tracked responsive headline' recipe from every AI hero.
code_tells.fix: Scale, weight and tracking should come from YOUR type scale, not the template's.

code_tells.name: Untouched shadcn defaults
code_tells.explain: A full shadcn install with the stock radius and colour tokens. shadcn is fine - unchanged defaults are what make every AI site look identical.
code_tells.fix: Change the tokens: your own --primary, your own --radius, one token the defaults don't have.

code_tells.name: Icon tile above card heading
code_tells.explain: The little rounded square holding an icon above every card title - 'the universal AI feature-card template'.
code_tells.fix: Ask what the icon adds. Usually: nothing. Use a real screenshot, a number, or just the words.

code_tells.name: Twin hero CTAs
code_tells.explain: 'Get Started' next to 'Learn More' - the default button pair, and both labels tell the user nothing.
code_tells.fix: Name the action: 'Open an account', 'See pricing', 'Try the demo'.

code_tells.name: Round fake stats
code_tells.explain: Round unverifiable numbers ('10K+ users', '99.9% uptime'). On a new product they read as invented.
code_tells.fix: Real number or no number. 'Show more, claim less.'

code_tells.name: Side-stripe accent borders
code_tells.explain: Coloured left stripes on cards - 'almost as reliable a sign of AI design as em-dashes' - unless they encode real status.
code_tells.fix: Keep only where the colour MEANS something (error, warning). Delete decorative ones.

code_tells.name: Ghost card (border + big shadow)
code_tells.explain: A hairline border AND a big soft shadow on the same card - two competing depth systems at once.
code_tells.fix: Pick one: border OR shadow. Define 2-3 elevation levels and stick to them.

code_tells.name: min-h-screen on everything
code_tells.explain: Humans set full-height once, on the root. AI repeats it on every section.
code_tells.fix: Keep it on the root wrapper only. Let sections be as tall as their content.

code_tells.name: Tailwind-UI container fossil
code_tells.explain: The exact wrapper from old Tailwind UI examples. Mostly gone from modern AI output; legacy signal.
code_tells.fix: Harmless alone; only matters in combination.

code_tells.name: The SaaS section skeleton
code_tells.explain: features + pricing + testimonials + faq, always in the same order. Structure is where AI output converges hardest.
code_tells.fix: Cut every section that doesn't serve YOUR product. Reorder around what your visitor actually asks first.

code_tells.name: The cliche icon set
code_tells.explain: Sparkles + Zap + Shield + Rocket from lucide, usually in a 3-card grid. The default 'features' iconography.
code_tells.fix: Icons only where they clarify. Product screenshots beat icon grids.

code_tells.name: Emoji as UI icons
code_tells.explain: Emoji standing in for designed icons. Screen readers announce them literally ('sparkles rocket fire').
code_tells.fix: Use a consistent icon set with text labels, or plain text.

code_tells.name: Placeholder people
code_tells.explain: Fake people and fake avatars. On a real site this is the single most damaging tell.
code_tells.fix: Real testimonials with permission, or none. Never invent people.

code_tells.name: Fade-up-on-scroll everywhere
code_tells.explain: Every section fading in as you scroll. Research shows it delays and frustrates readers; the page is blank if JavaScript fails.
code_tells.fix: Animate at most the first hero view, once. Content should be readable with JavaScript off.

code_tells.name: hover:scale on everything
code_tells.explain: Cards growing on hover, sitewide. Fine once; a tell everywhere.
code_tells.fix: Keep hover feedback subtle (opacity, border) and only on truly clickable things.

code_tells.name: Pulse on static things
code_tells.explain: Pulsing dots implying 'live' where nothing is live.
code_tells.fix: Animate only when data actually changes.

code_tells.name: Marquee / animated gradient
code_tells.explain: Auto-scrolling logo strips and hue-shifting backgrounds demand attention and hide content.
code_tells.fix: A static row of real logos, or nothing.

code_tells.name: Untouched Compose template palette
code_tells.explain: These are the exact colour values Android Studio's Empty Activity template ships with. Three or more of them still in the file means nobody chose this palette. That is a scaffold left in place, not proof a model wrote the app - a person's first Android project looks identical.
code_tells.fix: Pick real colours for the product, then replace the values in ui/theme/Color.kt. Keep the names if you like; it is the values that give it away.

code_tells.name: Untouched Expo tabs scaffold
code_tells.explain: \"Tab One\" and #2f95dc are create-expo-app's own placeholders, and the chevron icon is the one the template puts on every tab. Two or more of them shipping together means the navigation was never designed. Same caveat as any scaffold tell: it says unfinished, not AI-written.
code_tells.fix: Name the tabs after what they do, give each one its own icon, and replace the tint colour.

code_tells.name: Tailwind default palette inside mobile code
code_tells.explain: Three or more of Tailwind's stock hex values hard-coded in a Dart or Kotlin file. Tailwind is a web framework: these numbers have no way of reaching a native file except through a model that writes web code by default. Measured across 12 generated mobile repos and a 413-file human-built control, where it appeared zero times.
code_tells.fix: Generate a palette for the app and use the tokens. If the project genuinely uses NativeWind or a shared Tailwind config, say so - this rule is scoped to native files for that reason.

code_tells.name: Untouched Expo default scaffold
patterns: Edit src/app/index\.tsx to edit this screen\.
code_tells.explain: These are create-expo-app's DEFAULT template, which is what a bare `npx create-expo-app` produces - a different scaffold from the tabs template MB2 covers, sharing none of its literals. `hint-row` and `web-badge` are the template's own guided-tour components, the tabIcons PNGs are its placeholder tab art, and the rest is its placeholder copy. Two or more surviving together means nobody has touched the starting screen. Same caveat as any scaffold tell: it says unfinished, not AI-written.
code_tells.fix: Delete the tour components and the placeholder copy, replace the two tab icons with your own art, and name the tabs after what they do.

copy_tells.notes: transformation_verbs and vague_ctas are HIGH false-positive: humans wrote marketese long before AI (documented back to 1997). They score 1 point each (cap 4) on the AI axis but always appear on the craft axis as weak copy. ai_cadence items score only on density: 2+ distinct hits.
copy_tells.ai_cadence_comment: Era-tagged, because AI vocabulary turns over about every 12-18 months. Structural phrases in ai_cadence are shapes, not fashions, and hold across eras. The 2023 bucket is kept as a legacy signal: Wikipedia's Signs of AI writing records that 'delve' dropped off sharply in 2025. The 2025 bucket needs a higher bar than the others because those are ordinary marketing words - flagging 'enhance' on its own would be wrong far more often than right. Re-check by 2027-03. Source: M11.

craft_checks.comment: These are quality/accessibility failures, NOT proof of AI. They feed the craft score. Thresholds are cited in reference/accessibility.md.

checks.name: Likely low-contrast body text
checks.explain: Light grey body text usually fails the 4.5:1 contrast minimum (WCAG 2.2, rule 1.4.3).
checks.fix: Darken to at least gray-600 on white (or gray-300 on near-black), then verify with a contrast checker.

checks.name: Animations without a reduced-motion path
checks.explain: The site animates but never checks the user's 'reduce motion' setting (WCAG 2.3.3 technique C39). Motion can cause dizziness and nausea.

checks.name: Focus outline removed
checks.explain: Keyboard users can't see where they are (WCAG 2.4.7).
checks.fix: Never remove the outline without a visible replacement (e.g. focus-visible:ring-2).

checks.name: Justified body text
checks.explain: Justified text creates uneven 'rivers' of space that are harder to read, especially for dyslexic readers (BDA guide; WCAG 1.4.8).

checks.name: Tiny body text
checks.explain: Lots of very small text. Body copy should be at least 16px (BDA guide).
checks.fix: Reserve text-xs for true fine print; body at text-base (16px) or larger.

checks.name: Uppercase running text
checks.explain: Uppercase removes the word shapes dyslexic readers rely on (BDA guide). Fine for tiny labels, not for sentences.
checks.fix: Use sentence case for anything longer than a word or two.

ai_bands: leaning generic - fix the strongest findings
reads as AI-generated - rework before shipping
scoring.rule: No single non-provenance tell can push a page past a band boundary on its own; scoring is capped so bands are only crossed by co-occurrence. Provenance hits are reported separately as near-proof.
scoring.library_note: library_misuse findings score on the AI axis and are reported in their own section. Correct use of any of the nine libraries scores zero.

library_misuse.comment: Signatures for MISUSE of the nine ported libraries. Sources: reference/libraries/*.md, read from the live docs 2026-09-04. These score on the AI axis because each one is a documented route to a register tell. Correct use of the same library scores nothing.

rules.name: animate.css entrance carpet
rules.explain: Four or more animate.css entrance classes on one page. Every section fading in is the single most recognisable AI-motion tell, and the page is blank if JavaScript or the class fails.
rules.fix: Keep at most one entrance, on the hero, playing once. Delete the rest.

rules.name: animate.css infinite decoration
rules.explain: animate__infinite loops forever. Looping motion with no state behind it is decoration, and it is an attention trap for ADHD readers.
rules.fix: Remove it. Animate only when something actually changes.

rules.name: animate.css attention-seeker classes
rules.explain: Attention-seeker animations shake, wobble or flash the interface. They read as dated and they can trigger vestibular symptoms.
rules.fix: Use a colour or border change to draw attention instead.

rules.name: GSAP infinite tween
rules.explain: An infinite GSAP tween. Usually a marquee, a float or a pulse: motion that proves nothing except that the page is animating.
rules.fix: Delete it, or tie the tween to real state (loading, live data).

rules.name: GSAP bounce/elastic easing
rules.explain: Overshoot easing on interface elements. Fine for a physical object, dated on a button or card.
rules.fix: Use a plain ease-out under 300ms for interface motion.

rules.name: ScrollTrigger reveal carpet
rules.explain: Scroll-triggered reveals applied in bulk. Research shows this delays task-focused readers, and content is invisible until scrolled into view.
rules.fix: Reveal the hero once at most. Body content should be readable immediately.

rules.name: Scroll hijacking
rules.explain: Smooth-scroll libraries override the user's native scrolling. On a reading page this breaks scroll speed expectations, keyboard paging and anchor jumps.
rules.fix: Remove it on content pages. If the page genuinely IS a scroll experience, gate it behind prefers-reduced-motion and keep keyboard scrolling native.

rules.name: anime.js scroll-reveal density
rules.explain: Three or more anime.js onScroll() animations. Same carpet problem as ScrollTrigger.

rules.name: anime.js infinite loop
rules.explain: An infinite anime.js loop, usually a decorative float or pulse.
rules.fix: Remove it, or drive it from real changing data.

rules.name: Decorative canvas / particle field
rules.explain: A WebGL canvas behind content. Screen readers see nothing inside a canvas, and a particle field is the clearest 'we had nothing to show' signal there is.
rules.fix: Delete it. If the canvas carries real content (a game, a data view), give it a text alternative and keyboard access.

rules.name: SplitText accessibility disabled
rules.explain: Text split into characters or words with the accessibility fallback turned off. Screen readers then read the heading letter by letter, or not at all.
rules.fix: Leave accessible:true (the default), or do not split the text.

rules.name: Leaflet map without attribution
rules.explain: A Leaflet map with no attribution string. Tile providers require attribution, and OpenStreetMap has a usage policy with real limits.
rules.fix: Add the attribution option your tile provider requires. See reference/libraries/maps-forms.md.
